quote: Theorem 3.1. Let X, Y1 and Y2 be continuous and non-negative rv's corresponding to survival functions F̄(·), H̄(·; θ1, k1) and H̄(·; θ2, k2), respectively. Moreover, let {0 < θ1 ≤ 1, θ2 ≥ 1}. Then: (i) If X ∈ UIPLR (IPLR, ILR), then Y1 ⪯plr↑ (⪯plr, ⪯lr↑) Y2. (ii) If X ∈ DIPLR (DLR), then Y1 ⪯plr↓ (⪯lr↓) Y2. (iii) If X ∈ UIPFR (IPFR, IFR), then Y1 ⪯phr↑ (⪯phr, ⪯hr↑) Y2. (iv) If X ∈ DIPFR (DFR), then Y1 ⪯phr↓ (⪯hr↓) Y2.
model: Harris family distributions with different tilt parameters
family: Harris family H(x; θ, k) with baseline F; {θ1 ≤ 1, θ2 ≥ 1}
compared: two Harris rvs in proportional/shifted lr and hr orders under proportional ageing properties of the baseline

hypotheses.text: 0 < θ1 ≤ 1, θ2 ≥ 1; baseline X in UIPLR/IPLR/ILR, DIPLR/DLR, UIPFR/IPFR/IFR, or DIPFR/DFR class

conclusion.direction: Y1 ⪯· Y2 (proportional or shifted likelihood-ratio / hazard-rate orders)

ambiguity: OCR renders ⪯ as ¬; proportional and shifted orders are defined in the paper's Section 2.

quote: Theorem 3.2. Let Y1 and Y2 be rv's corresponding to the df's H(·; θ1, k1) and H(·; θ2, k2), respectively. If {0 < θ1 ≤ 1, θ2 ≥ 1} or {0 < θ1 ≤ θ2, k1 = k2 = k}, then Y1 ⪯lr Y2.
compared: two Harris rvs in likelihood-ratio order by tilt
ambiguity: Remark 3.1 corrects Theorem 2.3 of the cited Marshall–Olkin result: valid only with θ2 ≥ θ1 (not θ1 ≥ θ2).

quote: Corollary 3.1. Let Y1 and Y2 be rv's corresponding to df's H(·; θ1, k1) and H(·; θ2, k2), respectively. If {0 < θ1 ≤ 1, θ2 ≥ 1} or {0 < θ1 ≤ θ2, k1 = k2 = k}, then Y1 ⪯hr (⪯rh, ⪯st, ⪯E) Y2.
compared: two Harris rvs in hazard-rate, reversed-hazard-rate, usual stochastic and expectation orders
ambiguity: ⪯E denotes expectation order in the paper's notation.

quote: Theorem 3.3. Let Y1 and Y2 be rv's corresponding to Harris family df's H(·; θ1, k) and H(·; θ2, k), respectively. Then Y1 ⪯AI Y2 provided that θ1 > θ2.
model: Harris family distributions with common k
compared: two Harris rvs in ageing intensity order by tilt

quote: Theorem 4.1. X1 ⪯st X2 if and only if Y1 ⪯st Y2.
compared: usual stochastic order of baselines equivalent to that of Harris images

hypotheses.text: Y1, Y2 are the Harris transforms of X1, X2 with the same θ, k

quote: Theorem 4.2. (i) Assume that θ ≥ 1. If X1 ⪯phr↑ (⪯phr, ⪯hr↑, ⪯hr) X2, then Y1 ⪯phr↑ (⪯phr, ⪯hr↑, ⪯hr) Y2. (ii) Assume that 0 < θ ≤ 1. If Y1 ⪯phr↑ (⪯phr, ⪯hr↑, ⪯hr) Y2, then X1 ⪯phr↑ (⪯phr, ⪯hr↑, ⪯hr) X2.
compared: preservation/reflection of proportional and shifted hazard-rate orders between baseline and Harris rvs

hypotheses.text: θ ≥ 1 for forward preservation; 0 < θ ≤ 1 for converse

conclusion.direction: X1 <=· X2 iff Y1 <=· Y2 (direction controlled by θ)

quote: Counterexample 4.1. Let X1 and X2 be two rv's having the Erlang distributions with survival functions F̄1(x) = (1 + 2x)e^{−2x}, F̄2(x) = (x + 1)e^{−x} and hazard rates rF1(x) = 4x/(1 + 2x), rF2(x) = x/(x + 1), for x > 0, respectively. So, X1 ⪯hr↑ X2. However, Figure 1 shows that for some 0 < θ < 1, t > 0 and some x > 0, rH1(x + t; θ, k) ≯ rH2(x; θ, k) or, equivalently, H̄2(x; θ, k)/H̄1(x + t; θ, k) is not increasing in x, i.e., the up hazard rate order is not preserved by transformation to the Harris family when 0 < θ < 1.
compared: up hazard-rate order of baselines does not transfer to Harris images for θ < 1
ambiguity: Adapted from counterexample 3.2 of a cited work; the failure is shown graphically.

quote: Corollary 4.1. Let X1 and X2 be two rv's with mean residual life (mrl) functions m1 and m2 and Harris family rv's Y1 and Y2 having mrl functions m*1 and m*2, respectively, such that m1(t)/m2(t) increases in t. If X1 ⪯mrl X2, then Y1 ⪯mrl Y2 provided that θ ≥ 1. The orders are reversed if m*1(t)/m*2(t) increases in t and 0 < θ ≤ 1.
family: any baselines with mrl ratio condition
compared: mrl order of baselines transfers to Harris rvs (θ ≥ 1) or reverses (θ ≤ 1)

hypotheses.text: m1/m2 increasing (θ ≥ 1 case); m*1/m*2 increasing (θ ≤ 1 case)

conclusion.direction: X1 <=mrl X2 ⇒ Y1 <=mrl Y2 (θ≥1); reversed for θ≤1

quote: Theorem 4.3. Assume that X1 and X2 are non-negative rv's. For all k > 0, if X1 ⪯AI X2 and X1 ⪯hr X2, then Y1 ⪯AI Y2 provided that θ > 1.
compared: ageing intensity order preserved under Harris transformation for θ > 1

hypotheses.text: X1 ⪯AI X2 and X1 ⪯hr X2; θ > 1

quote: Theorem 4.4. The following orders are preserved by transformation from a baseline distribution to its corresponding Harris family and vice versa. (i) convex transform order, (ii) star order, (iii) super-additive order, (iv) dispersive order.
model: Harris transformation, common tilt (any θ, k)
compared: c, *, su and disp orders equivalent between baselines and Harris images

hypotheses.text: H2^{-1}∘H1 = F2^{-1}∘F1 (Lemma 4.1), so transform-based order conditions coincide

conclusion.direction: X1 <=· X2 iff Y1 <=· Y2 for each of the four orders

quote: Corollary 4.2. If X1 ⪯Lorenz X2, then Y1 ⪯Lorenz Y2 provided that the function F2^{-1}(x)/F1^{-1}(x) is increasing for all x > 0.
compared: Lorenz order preserved under Harris transformation
ambiguity: Via star order (star ⇒ Lorenz) and Theorem 4.4(ii).

quote: Corollary 5.1. Let θ > 1 (0 < θ < 1). (i) The IFRA (DFRA) characteristic is preserved by transformation to the Harris family. (ii) The NBU (NWU) characteristic is preserved by transformation to the Harris family.
family: IFRA/DFRA and NBU/NWU baselines (X compared with exponential X1 via star and super-additive orders)
compared: ageing-class membership transfers from baseline X to Harris transform Y

hypotheses.text: θ > 1 (IFRA/NBU case) or 0 < θ < 1 (DFRA/NWU case); exponential reference X1
